Team —

Quick ask: we're two weeks from onsite for the Senior LLM Serving candidate (J. Smith) and we need a short calibration so interviewers and the bar-raiser are aligned on scope, leveling signals, and any hard gating criteria. Recruiter Jenny is looped for schedule constraints.

High-level background: this role will sit on the Serving runtime team and should own productionization patterns (kernel selection, KV cache behavior, batching tradeoffs), system-level reliability (SLOs/observability), and partner-facing rollout decisions (model variants, routing policies). We agreed IC5 / Senior expectations, but I'd like us to be explicit about must-have vs nice-to-have signals so debriefs are crisp.

Proposed agenda for a 30-minute sync:
- One-sentence role scope anchors (what to gate on)
- Top 4 interview focus areas (what to probe)
- Leveling signals (pass/fail vs stretch examples)
- Quick rubric tweak and interviewer assignments
- Final check on schedule conflicts / interview overlap with other slates

Attachments: JD, current rubric draft, candidate resume (light redactions). Please review before we meet. If you can't make the quick sync, reply inline with your top-3 anchors.

Preferred times today: 10:30-11:00 or 11:45-12:15 PT. I'll set the calendar for whichever gets most thumbs up.

Thanks —
Olga
Director, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: Alignment: Senior LLM Serving — scope anchors & deconflict (Aug hiring slate)

Olga — thanks for kicking this off. I'm the bar-raiser here and want to be explicit about two gating items I care about:

1) Production judgment under constrained budgets: candidate should articulate concrete strategies (e.g., KV caching eviction policies, prefix caching heuristics) and tradeoffs with quantization/batching. High-level hand-wavy answers are a red flag.
2) System-level debugging: ability to trace a tail-latency incident from the runtime through scheduler/kernel selection to infra and explain mitigations and instrumentation choices.

Top-4 focus areas I'd ask interviewers to probe:
- Runtime architecture and latency troubleshooting (30%)
- Cost/efficiency tradeoffs and quantization impacts (25%)
- Cross-team rollout & compatibility decisions (15%)
- Mentoring/ownership examples (30%)

Leveling signals:
- Senior (IC5) should have 2+ examples of making a tradeoff that materially changed cost/latency and be able to quantify impact.
- Stretch to staff (IC6) would require org-level influence and measurable product/infra outcomes.

Rubric tweak: add a short section for "quantitative impact" (0/1/2 scale) and an explicit tie-breaker: if two candidates are close on technical signal, prefer the one with stronger cross-team deployment/rollout experience.

I can join the 11:45 slot if that works.

—Markus
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime (Bar-raiser)

- Please avoid overlapping kernel-level deep dives in two separate loops — makes the candidate repeat technical depth without new context. If Markus covers kernel debugging, I'll emphasize rollout/PRD ownership.

I've attached an updated rubric (interview-rubric-v2.xlsx) — small changes per Markus' quantitative-impact suggestion and a short interviewer checklist.

I'll be there at 11:45.
